images.text: Kristi: Okay, things are under control so far. Adam is setting up the tables and says he will arrange for a second entrance. The bookstore has an armchair that we can use and Denise said she will bring a rug from home that we can have the kids sit on. The copies of the book are here. I'm glad I thought to order those really early. I'll get Adam to unpack those and stack them on the table. He can also set up a few chairs in case there are some parents who want to sit. Denise will bring her camera so we can get lots of photos. I'll just check my e-mail to see if anyone else has confirmed or cancelled. It looks like all the social media people I invited are coming so that's great. Now I just need to call the caterer. I've been so busy that I forgot to confirm with the caterers.

Mitch: Hello? Kate's Catering, this is Mitch speaking.
Kristi: Hi Mitch. This is Kristi Lenard. I'm calling to confirm the catering order that is to be delivered to The Bookworm tonight at 5:00 p.m. Are we on track with that?
Mitch: Yes, Kristi. We've got two fruit platters, two veggie platters, two dessert platters and three kids pizza platters. We're bringing 60 cans of juice and pop, and tea and coffee in urns for 40 people. I also see that we are picking up your wine order. Were you informed that there is an extra charge for that?
Kristi: Yes, that's no problem. You've been so helpful that I'm happy to pay for that.
Mitch: We will supply wine glasses and openers.
Kristi: That's great. Thank you! This event has come up so quickly that I haven't had time to organize glasses.

Mitch: Kristi, is it okay if we drop off the order at 4:45 p.m.? We are so busy today that we are having a few delivery time conflicts.
Kristi: Yes, that's no problem. I will meet you at the entrance.
Mitch: Great. See you at 4:45. Bye.
Kristi: Bye.
Kristi: Okay, that's taken care of. Speaking of food, I should eat something. I've been so focused on this event that I forgot to eat!

You use so ... that to link a cause with a result. When you want to be clear about the cause of something, this is a good way to refer to it.
The bus was so slow that I was late for my interview.
You normally use an adjective or adverb after so.
It all happened so quickly that I never had a chance to fully absorb what was going on.
In formal English, you can put so ... that at the beginning of the sentence and put the verb before the object.
So slow was the bus that I was late for my interview.
I've been so busy that I forgot to confirm with the caterers.
You've been so helpful that I'm happy to pay for that.
This event has come up so quickly that I haven't had time to organize glasses.
We are so busy today that we are having a few delivery time conflicts.
I've been so focused on this event that I forgot to eat!
Will to Express Willingness or Intention
When you make a decision at the moment of speaking for the future, you use the modal will. This is in the context of saying that you are willing to do something or that you intend to do something.

We use WILL / WON'T to express that someone is / is not not willing to do something in the present.
Examples:
Richard is a nice guy; he will always help you if you are in trouble. (willingness)

Mary will translate for you - she speaks French. (willingness)

Fernanda is mad at me; she will not (won't) talk to me. (unwillingness)

I'll do it — I don't mind. (willingness)
I won't be coming later. (intention)
I'll call you later. (intention)
He will arrange for a second entrance.
Denise said she will bring a rug from home that we can have the kids sit on.
Denise will bring her camera so we can get lots of photos.
We will supply wine glasses and openers.
